title: Power Apps: model-driven apps as Business Applications in Work IQ
summary: Hold: the claim that operation rates are unpublished overlooks Microsoft's published Work IQ Tool API rate. The Agent 365 overview also no longer supports the statement that the Copilot Studio integration is preview; distinguish the generally available integration from its preview Business apps workload.

claims.claim: The November 2026 plan to enable existing environments has been deferred.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptionshas been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: No replacement date is stated for enabling existing environments.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment enable disable API PowerShell settings; opened Business Applications in Work IQ default settings and Manage participation. The deferral notice supplies no replacement date.

claims.quote: Turn on Dataverse intelligence (Work IQ) for agents and AI experiences | When On, allows reusable business context business skills to be used by your agents. | Off

claims.claim: Consumption is a documented licensing model for accessing this feature.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses consumption billing.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Usage and billing follow the consuming experience rather than a dedicated Business Applications cost category.
claims.quote: For Business Applications in Work IQ, you track cost by the experiences people use rather than by a dedicated business applications category.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ in Copilot Studio uses the Microsoft Copilot harness and Copilot Credits for usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ in Copilot Studio is powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, which uses Copilot Credits for usage-based billing.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ consumption supporting a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.
claims.quote: Copilot Cowork: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Direct calls by coding agents or custom integrations are reported under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.claim: No extra licence specific to these Business Applications operations is stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications Work IQ pricing credits operation license; read the feature user and cost pages, Work IQ overview, API licensing excerpt and Microsoft's Work IQ GA announcement. No separate Business Applications operations licence was stated.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A credit rate for Business Applications operations through Work IQ API is not yet published.
claims.quote: Work IQ API consumption consists of two parts: variable charge for query-style consumption (grounding, retrieval, and reasoning) and a static usage component for actions and tools invoked through Work IQ. Static | Work IQ Tool API | 0.1 Copilot Credits per API call
claims.fix: Narrow the repeated rate-absence statements to: 'The feature's cost page gives no fixed price per Business Applications prompt; total cost depends on the consuming experience and work performed.' Remove 'Not yet published' and the question asking for an unpublished Work IQ API operation rate. Microsoft publishes a general Work IQ Tool API rate, not a fixed price per business-app prompt, at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/licensing/news/work-iq-general-availability.

claims.claim: Work IQ API consumption can mix Microsoft 365 and business applications context, so it is not a Business Applications-only breakdown.
claims.quote: Work IQ API consumption can include both Microsoft 365 productivity context and business applications context. Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.claim: For Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, the applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: The applicable entitlement includes business-data grounding in the licensed chat scenario. You don't pay extra for it as a Work IQ API interaction.

claims.claim: One request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so cost per prompt varies.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.claim: Work IQ API consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: The environment Work IQ switch is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: Select Manage, and select the environment. Select Settings > Product > Features. Locate Work IQ. Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: An environment administrator can manage the environment Work IQ setting.
claims.quote: Use the environment-level setting to manage business skills, semantic modeling, and access to Dataverse data through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, Research, and Agent Builder. You need an environment administrator account.

claims.claim: Enabling environment features is separate from allowing Work IQ to reason over the environment's data.
claims.quote: Enabling these features in an environment is a separate decision from allowing Work IQ to reason over that environment's data.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for the environment Work IQ switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ environment enable disable API PowerShell settings; opened Manage participation, default settings and Manage feature settings. Results document the UI, not an operation setting this environment switch.

claims.claim: The audience control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings. In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Audience options are All users, Specific groups and No users, with All users the default.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select No users. To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default. To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups

claims.claim: The tenant-level audience setting needs a tenant administrator account.
claims.quote: Use the tenant-level setting to manage whether Power Apps and Dynamics 365 data can be used in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat across the tenant. You need a tenant administrator account.

claims.claim: The audience control is described for Microsoft 365 Copilot, but its applicability to the Copilot Studio tool is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications Copilot Studio audience tenant setting; opened default settings, Manage AI experience access and Work IQ in Copilot Studio. The audience instructions name Microsoft 365 Copilot/Chat, not the Studio tool.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second row and closing paragraph
claims.claim: An API or PowerShell equivalent for the Business Applications Copilot audience setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications data Copilot tenant setting API PowerShell; opened default settings and Manage AI experience access; read tenant-settings search results. No operation for this audience setting was found.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. Select Work IQ MCP. Review its current availability. To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: The ability to allow or disallow tooling and MCP servers might not yet be available in the reader's region.
claims.quote: The ability to allow or disallow tooling and MCP servers in the Microsoft 365 admin center might not be available in your region yet.

claims.claim: The cited feature guide enables App Access at Power Platform admin center > Security > Identity & access > App Access Control > environment > Enable > Save.
claims.quote: Select Security > Identity & access. Select App Access Control. Select the environment in which you want to enable app access. Select Enable, and then select Save.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Scope: Roles; Governance controls: fourth row
claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator is the documented role for application-access settings.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator role to work with application-access settings in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data; App Access governs application access.
claims.quote: App Access addresses application access to the underlying environment data. Work IQ participation settings serve a different purpose and don't prevent agentic access.

claims.claim: PATCH <organization-url>/api/data/v9.2/applications(<application-id>) with access set to 1 blocks that application.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/applications; Primary key: applicationid; Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE; access | Edm.Int32 | Application Access; 0 | Allowed; 1 | Blocked
claims.fix: Set controls[3].api.call and the rendered call to 'PATCH <organization-url>/api/data/v9.2/applications(<application-id>)'. In the note, write 'The request body sets access to 1 (Blocked), or 0 (Allowed).' Remove the headers and body from the displayed call.

claims.claim: App Access must be enabled before using its per-application block configuration.
claims.quote: If you set some apps to Allowed or Blocked, you don't need to remove the setting when the app access control feature is turned off to Disabled. There are no app restrictions in this environment.

claims.claim: Setting the application's access property to 0 allows it.
claims.quote: access | Edm.Int32 | Application Access; Default options: 0 | Allowed; 1 | Blocked

claims.claim: The general App Access article requires a managed environment.
claims.quote: Verify that your environment is a managed environment. Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: The general App Access article gives environment > Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled > application > Block > Save.
claims.quote: Select the Set up app access control button. Select Enabled in the Access control dropdown list. Select a Dataverse application, then select one of these options, located above the grid: Allow ... Block ... Select Save.

claims.claim: The feature-specific guide says to return to the environment after Enable and Save to select applications to block.
claims.quote: Select Enable, and then select Save. Return to the environment and select the applications you want to block from accessing the environment.

claims.claim: App participation is at Power Apps > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps.
claims.quote: Select Apps. Find the app that you want to manage, and then select Edit. On the app navigation bar, select Settings. Select Features. Set Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps to On or Off.

claims.claim: Makers save and publish the app after changing its Copilot setting.
claims.quote: Makers can enable or disable Microsoft Copilot for a specific model-driven app. ... Select Save and then publish the app for the changes to take effect.

claims.claim: The user page requires m365copilotmodelappenabled to be Default or On.

claims.claim: The Dataverse SaveSettingValue action creates or updates an app-setting override using AppUniqueName, SettingName and Value.
claims.quote: Creates or updates app/organization level override. AppUniqueName: Model-driven app unique name (Optional). SettingName: Setting definition unique name (Required). Value: Overridden value that needs to be set (Required).
claims.fix: Set controls[4].api.call and the rendered call to 'POST <organization-url>/api/data/v9.2/SaveSettingValue'. Add to its note: 'The request body sets AppUniqueName, SettingName (m365copilotmodelappenabled), and Value.' Remove the headers and body from the displayed call.

claims.claim: Environment Maker or System Customizer can configure app-level participation.

claims.quote: Open your agent. In the agent designer toolbar, select the ellipsis (...), and then select Settings. In the Agent settings dialog, select Work IQ. Under Preview workloads, turn on Enable preview workloads.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope
claims.claim: Work IQ respects existing Power Platform permissions and grants no additional business-data access.
claims.quote: Work IQ respects your existing Power Platform security permissions. You can only select environments and applications, view data, and perform actions that your permissions allow. ... Work IQ doesn't grant additional access to business data.

claims.claim: Enabling Work IQ might send data from a FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365 outside the applicable authorization boundary.
claims.quote: Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.claim: Users need access to the Work IQ experience and permission for the environment, model-driven app and business data.
claims.quote: You need access to the Work IQ experience where you want to use Business Applications. ... You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.claim: The user page's prerequisites list experience access, environment enablement, the app setting and data permissions, but name no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications Work IQ pricing credits operation license; opened Use Business Applications in Work IQ and read its complete Prerequisites section. Its four prerequisites do not name a licence.

claims.claim: Learn troubleshooting advises checking that Work IQ is enabled for a missing environment.
claims.quote: Ask your administrator whether Work IQ is enabled for the environment.

claims.claim: Learn troubleshooting advises checking that the app setting is On or Default and the app is published.
claims.quote: Ask the app maker whether Enable Microsoft 365 Copilot in model-driven apps is set to On or Default and the app is published.

claims.claim: Learn advises checking Dataverse security roles and record access when an app appears but data is missing.
claims.quote: If the app appears but data is missing, confirm your Dataverse security roles and record access.

claims.where: summary; Governance controls: settings cascade; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Business Applications participation has cascading tenant, environment and app settings.
claims.quote: You manage Business Applications in Work IQ through a cascading set of settings at three levels: Microsoft 365 admin center (tenant level) ... Power Platform admin center (environment level) ... Power Apps maker portal (app level)

claims.claim: Turning off the tenant setting prevents sharing between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse even when an app is configured to share.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, data isn't shared between Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and Dataverse, even if an app is configured to share data.

claims.claim: The AI-experience access article describes the tenant control as the setting for business applications availability.
claims.quote: Open the setting for business applications availability in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The general Agent 365 management article includes Registry in the route Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. ... Select Block to restrict the server across your organization

claims.where: Open questions: Work IQ MCP tenant policy
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy disallows mutation operations by default for Microsoft 365 resource paths.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.where: Open questions: Work IQ MCP tenant policy
claims.claim: It is not confirmed whether the documented Microsoft 365 MCP mutation policy also governs writes to Business Applications data.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ Business Applications mutation policy; opened Policy governance for Work IQ MCP and read the tool-reference excerpt. They describe Microsoft 365/Graph resource paths, without explicitly placing Business Applications writes in that policy's scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Confirmation behaviour when a Copilot Studio agent runs without a person present is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Applications Work IQ confirmation unattended autonomous agent; opened Use Business Applications in Work IQ and Work IQ in Copilot Studio. Confirmation is documented for conversation users, not for unattended execution.

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator enables Work IQ for the environment.
claims.quote: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is not currently available in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.claim: The cost rating is variable because documented access uses usage-based Copilot Credits billing.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing (UBB) charges for consumption rather than simply enabling a feature. Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.
